channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: De Travis Scott a Ana Maria Braga: jogo do Brasil na Copa reúne famosos
item.description: Brazil kicked off its 2026 World Cup campaign against Morocco in New Jersey, with celebrities including Ana Maria Braga, Travis Scott, Tom Brady, Neymar, Ronaldo, Maisa, and Giovanna Lancellotti in attendance. The match highlighted the intersection of sports and pop culture, drawing global attention.

item.title: Na Copa do Mundo, prefeito de Nova York exalta ex-craque do Brasil
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani praised Brazilian football legend Sócrates during a speech about Brazil's 2026 World Cup opener, highlighting his captaincy in the 1982 tournament and his leadership in the Corinthians Democracy movement, which resisted Brazil's military dictatorship. Mamdani, a political opponent of Donald Trump, linked Sócrates' legacy to Brazil's democratic struggle and recommended venues for fans to watch the Brazil vs. Morocco match.

item.title: Casado ou solteiro? O status dos jogadores da seleção na Copa do Mundo
item.description: The text examines the marital status of the 26 players called up by Carlo Ancelotti for the Brazilian national team in the 2026 World Cup, noting that most are married or in stable relationships, with few singles and only one case lacking information (Danilo Santos). Reported by the GENTE column, it reveals players’ personal lives off the pitch, contrasting with the team’s collective focus on winning a sixth title.

item.title: Eduardo sugere rompimento com Novo após crítica de Zema
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL-SP) advocated for a break between bolsonarism and the New Party after criticisms from presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo-MG) toward Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). Zema, in an interview with Brasil Paralelo, urged caution regarding individuals close to those under investigation, which Eduardo interpreted as politically motivated envy. Eduardo has since publicly endorsed federal deputy Júlia Zanatta (PL-SC) as vice-presidential candidate, indicating an internal realignment within the right-wing coalition.

item.title: Lula envia mensagem a Carlo Ancelotti e faz apelo à seleção na Copa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sent a public message to coach Carlo Ancelotti hours before Brazil's World Cup opener against Morocco. In a social media video, Lula urged the team to play with determination, unity, and in the interest of the Brazilian people, encouraging them to play with soul and shoot at every opportunity, stating that Ancelotti would become a hero if he secured victory.

item.title: Reforma do Judiciário: necessária, mas com muitos pontos silenciados
item.description: Minister Flávio Dino's article advocates for a Brazilian judiciary reform aimed at strengthening the STF, not weakening it, by leveraging the current crisis to improve decision-making efficiency and quality. It rejects the notion of 'excess of Justice,' pointing to the massive backlog of over 75 million pending cases in 2026 and extreme delays in areas like fiscal executions and crimes against life. The proposal emphasizes structural measures — such as stricter appellate filters, specialized chambers, and clear jurisdictional rules — over rhetorical calls for judicial restraint.

item.title: 'Dark Horse': produtora diz que filme sobre Jair Bolsonaro custou R$ 75 milhões
item.description: Go UP Entertainment told the court that the film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro's life, cost R$ 75 million, with R$ 54 million spent abroad and R$ 20.9 million in Brazil. A defense expert report claims the funds came from private investments, specifically the Havengate Development Fund LP, linked to Paulo Calixto, an ally of Eduardo Bolsonaro. The investigation examines whether public funds from a São Paulo City Hall contract with Instituto Conhecer Brasil — also tied to Karina Ferreira da Gama — were improperly used for the film's production.

item.title: A aposta do PT para derrubar PEC que reduz a maioridade penal
item.description: The PT leadership in the Chamber plans to use Deputy Patrus Ananias’ arguments to block the PEC reducing the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16, claiming it violates constitutional clauses, the principle of proportionality, and exposes minors to the adult prison system without proven effectiveness. The proposal was approved in the CCJ by 44 votes to 18 and now awaits a special committee appointed by Chamber President Hugo Motta. The PT also sees rejecting the PEC as a way to counter a campaign platform of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula’s main rival in the 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Rodrigo Prando na Crusoé: Soberania, violência e eleição
item.description: The article examines Brazil's 2026 electoral cycle, emphasizing the tension between formal democracy and its functional shortcomings, with a focus on the polarization between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro as central figures in debates over sovereignty, violence, and political legitimacy. It suggests that the recurrence of these names reflects a calcification of the political field, where ideological conflicts overshadow institutional innovation.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: nova pesquisa Datafolha mede ‘fator Trump’ na eleição presidencial
item.description: Datafolha will conduct a new national poll on the 2026 Brazilian presidential election from June 17–19, surveying 2,004 voters. The poll will measure voting intentions in both spontaneous and stimulated scenarios, featuring Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Romeu Zema, and Ronaldo Caiado, while also testing the potential impact of a Donald Trump endorsement on voter behavior, alongside assessments of the economy, public safety, electoral behavior, and social issues.

item.title: Carlos diz que Bolsonaro estava com sonolência e “não acordava”
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro said his father, Jair Bolsonaro, is in a prolonged state of drowsiness due to strong medication and did not wake up during his visit on Saturday, June 13, 2026. He lamented that his brother Flávio cannot attend Brazil’s opening match in the 2026 World Cup and criticized the rules of temporary house arrest, claiming they harm the former president’s health.

item.title: Genebra se blinda com tapumes temendo quebra-quebra no G7
item.description: Geneva, Switzerland, has heightened security with protective barriers on businesses, increased police presence, and border controls with France ahead of the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, due to fears of violent protests. The precautions stem from the 2003 G8 summit, when Geneva experienced looting and vandalism. The 2026 summit will host leaders including Lula, Macron, and Trump, with protests anticipated in Geneva on the Sunday before the summit.

item.title: Eduardo sugere rompimento total com Partido Novo após críticas de Zema a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro suggested a complete break with the Novo Party following criticisms from Romeu Zema, the party's pre-candidate for president, directed at Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL's pre-candidate and Eduardo's brother. The proposed rupture stems from Zema's remarks questioning Flávio Bolsonaro's stance, creating tension between the Bolsonaro allies and the Novo Party.

item.title: Como o primeiro ministro petista no TCU avaliou as ‘ressalvas’ às contas de Lula
item.description: Petist minister Odair Cunha of the TCU approved Lula's 2025 accounts with reservations, agreeing with the rapporteur's criticisms regarding revenue overestimation, state-owned enterprise deficits, and off-budget spending, while emphasizing advances such as 2.3% GDP growth, unemployment dropping to 5.1%, and the creation of 1.3 million formal jobs. He argued that the budget should serve the realization of fundamental rights, not just surplus targets, stressing the need to balance fiscal responsibility with social welfare promotion.

item.title: Cadê a nossa bandeira, o verde e amarelo? A polarização política comeu
item.description: The column mourns the absence of green and yellow Brazilian flags in public spaces during the 2026 World Cup, blaming political polarization that makes citizens fear being associated with ideological camps when expressing patriotism. The author argues that supporting the national team and flag should transcend party affiliations, social classes, or personal beliefs, calling for courageous leaders to encourage the use of Brazil’s colors without fear. It also highlights the unjust veto of Somali referee Omar Artan by the U.S., tied to Trump’s discriminatory policies, as a troubling sign of the international climate affecting the Cup’s spirit.

item.title: “Por mim rompia geral com o partido Novo”, diz Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro advocated for breaking the alliance between the PL and the Novo party following criticism from former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema toward Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, related to revelations involving Flávio and Daniel Vorcaro, former controller of Banco Master. The statement was made in an interview on Saturday, the 13th, reflecting internal tensions within the Bolsonarist base. Zema’s comments prompted a direct reaction from Eduardo, who said he would personally end the alliance with Novo.

item.title: Flávio visita Jair Bolsonaro e diz que ele está bem, após Michelle falar em piora do quadro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro visited former President Jair Bolsonaro and stated that he is well, contradicting recent remarks by former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro about a deterioration in his health. The visit took place on Saturday, the 13th, and reinforces a narrative of clinical stability despite public concerns.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro defende rompimento com o Novo após críticas de Zema a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro called for ending the alliance between the PL and the New Party after former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema criticized Flávio Bolsonaro for his alleged ties to Daniel Vorcaro, former controller of Banco Master. Eduardo accused Zema of acting out of political rivalry and claimed the criticism was motivated by Zema’s desire to occupy Flávio’s position in the conservative field. The incident highlights growing tensions between Bolsonarists and the New Party, with Eduardo now favoring deputy Júlia Zanatta as vice president in a Flávio Bolsonaro-led ticket.

item.title: Quem vai fazer o primeiro gol do Brasil na Copa do Mundo? Faça suas apostas no Palpiteiros
item.description: Brazil’s 2026 World Cup opener against Morocco arrives without a clear goal-scorer, as Estêvão — the team’s top scorer under Ancelotti — is injured and unavailable. Globo’s new game 'Palpiteiros', developed with the Instituto Locomotiva, lets users predict who will score Brazil’s first goal and how far the team will advance, awarding more points for less likely outcomes. Betting closes at 6:50 PM Brasília time, 10 minutes before kickoff.

item.title: Defesa é desafio da política externa do Brasil, diz assessor de Lula
item.description: Audo Faleiro, deputy chief advisor of the Special Advisory Office to President Lula, stated that defense is one of the main challenges of Brazil's foreign policy, due to U.S. military action in Venezuela and the growing international conflict landscape. He noted that while there is no immediate threat to Brazil's oil reserves or nuclear program, the country must decide whether to invest in defense, given the tension between the belief in national pacifism and the military asymmetry with potential adversaries. Beyond defense, Faleiro identified critical minerals and rare earths, digital sovereignty, transnational organized crime, regional integration, and integration with African nations as key priorities through 2030.

item.title: El Niño destrava R$ 337 milhões contra incêndios
item.description: The federal government announced an extraordinary credit of R$ 337 million for Ibama and ICMBio to prevent and combat forest fires, anticipating the effects of the 2026/2027 El Niño, which NOAA warns could be the strongest in modern history. President Lula stated that Brazil is, for the first time, preparing in advance to mitigate risks of wildfires and extreme climate events, emphasizing proactive government action.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro pede rompimento com o Novo em resposta a Zema
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro criticized former governor Romeu Zema for attacking Flávio Bolsonaro over his association with Daniel Vorcaro, linked to the Banco Master scandal, and suggested a sharp break between his family and the Novo Party. He accused Zema of envy and stated that, if it were up to him, he would sever ties entirely with the party. Although Zema was once close to the Bolsonaros and considered as a potential running mate for Flávio, he was distanced after criticizing Vorcaro, and now Júlia Zanatta is the Novo Party's leading candidate, endorsed by Eduardo.

item.title: Camilo Santana, do PT, apoia classificar PCC e CV como terroristas
item.description: Senator Camilo Santana (PT-CE) advocated for classifying the PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, following the U.S. example, and criticized the federal government’s rejection of the move as arbitrary. He disclosed his disagreement to President Lula, calling the presidential stance 'equivocated,' and stressed that combating crime must transcend partisanship. Santana also accused political rivals of exploiting security issues for electoral gain, citing Ceará as a case in point.

item.title: “A sonolência se prolongou”, diz Carluxo sobre Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro (PL) stated that former President Jair Bolsonaro has again experienced prolonged drowsiness after starting stronger medications for health issues, which hindered a court-authorized visit. He said he traveled from Santa Catarina to Brasília but was unable to meet his father due to the medical condition.

item.title: Em vídeo, Lula pede garra e alma à seleção brasileira antes de estreia na Copa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) urged the Brazilian national team to show grit and soul in a social media video posted hours before their World Cup 2026 opener against Morocco. He advised that coach Carlo Ancelotti should instruct the players to demonstrate these qualities throughout the tournament.

item.title: Após autorização de Moraes, Flávio visita Bolsonaro em prisão domiciliar
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro visited former President Jair Bolsonaro under house arrest, authorized by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, during lunchtime. He said his father is healthy and expressed sadness at not being able to watch the World Cup match with him. The visit takes place amid polling showing declining support for Flávio Bolsonaro against Lula in potential 2026 election scenarios.

item.title: Em encontro com empresários, Simone Tebet fez revelações surpreendente sobre Lula
item.description: Simone Tebet revealed that the Ministry of Planning, under her leadership, completed a 25-year strategic plan for Brazil with targets across all sectors, but President Lula never signed the decree to implement it, citing discomfort in doing so during his final year in office. She also opposed closed-list proportional representation in political reform, arguing it would enable nepotism and that Brazil lacks the maturity for such a system.

item.title: Por que Brasil x Marrocos está entre os jogos mais procurados da Copa
item.description: The Brazil vs. Morocco match at the 2026 World Cup is among the most sought-after games, with 75,000 tickets sold in advance — behind only the final and the opening match. It leads in hospitality suite sales, surpassing even the final, showing fans now prioritize premium experiences over just watching the game.

item.title: Lula aumenta viagens pelo País, mas número ainda é menor do que de Bolsonaro; veja destinos
item.description: Lula made 47 national trips between January and May 2024, visiting 34 cities in 13 states, while Bolsonaro made 54 trips in the same period of 2022, visiting 51 cities in 20 states. The current president prioritized the three largest electoral colleges (Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, and Salvador), which accounted for a third of his travels, and also focused on São Paulo state, the destination of 16 of his trips. Despite increased travel compared to previous years, Lula’s number of trips remains below Bolsonaro’s in 2022 and also below his own 2006 re-election campaign.

item.title: Carlos diz que Jair Bolsonaro piorou: "Sonolência se prolongou"
item.description: Former councilman Carlos Bolsonaro stated that his father, Jair Bolsonaro, has experienced prolonged drowsiness due to stronger medications prescribed for worsening health conditions. He said that during a scheduled visit between 8 a.m. and 10 a.m., Bolsonaro remained asleep almost the entire time, waking only at 9:55 a.m., allowing just five minutes of interaction. Carlos criticized the visitation restrictions imposed by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, claiming they harm the former president’s health and prevent his granddaughters from attending Brazil’s 2026 World Cup opener with him.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro visita o pai em prisão domiciliar em Brasília
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro visited his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest at the Solar de Brasília condominium on Saturday morning (June 13), accompanied by his wife and two minor daughters. The visit was authorized by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, who also ordered a prior inspection and banned cell phone use during the meeting. Jair Bolsonaro has been serving house arrest since March 27 for humanitarian reasons, with the term set to end on June 25, following his conviction for attempting a coup d'état.

item.title: Produtora diz que usou R$ 75 milhões em filme de Bolsonaro e recursos saíram de fundo nos EUA
item.description: A forensic report released by producer Karina Ferreira Gama states that the fictional film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro, cost R$ 75 million, all sourced from the U.S.-based Havengate fund, which is allied with Eduardo Bolsonaro. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro requested banker Daniel Vorcaro to contribute US$ 10.6 million (about R$ 61 million) to the fund, which financed over 80% of the production. The producer’s defense uses the report to refute allegations of misappropriation of public funds from São Paulo City Hall.

item.title: Novo tenta consolidar candidatura de Zema, mas mantém pontes com PL nos estados
item.description: The New Party is positioning Romeu Zema’s gubernatorial candidacy as a right-wing alternative to Bolsonarism for the 2026 presidential race, while maintaining strategic alliances with the PL party at the state level to strengthen its congressional presence. The party aims to elect between 12 and 20 federal deputies, backed by a budget of up to R$90 million and gains from the 2024 municipal elections. Its strategy includes running full slates in most states and leveraging Zema’s potential national poll performance to boost proportional candidates nationwide.

item.title: Nunes Marques rejeita pedido para barrar filme sobre Bolsonaro durante eleições
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques of the TSE rejected a request by allies of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to block the screening of the film "Dark Horse", which focuses on former President Jair Bolsonaro, during the 2026 electoral period. The decision, published on Friday the 12th, found no legal basis to censor the film in the context of the election campaign.

item.title: Antes de ser revogada, 'taxa das blusinhas' rendeu mais de R$ 2 bilhões ao governo em 2026
item.description: The 'blusinhas tax', a 20% federal import tax on international parcels under US$ 50, was revoked in mid-May 2026 after collecting R$ 2.13 billion from January to mid-May, a 15.4% increase compared to the same period in 2025. Although the federal tax was abolished, states continue to levy ICMS on these imports at rates between 17% and 20%. The measure, initially supported by national industry and officials like Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, faced criticism from consumers for raising prices on low-cost goods and reducing the appeal of platforms such as Shein, Shopee, and AliExpress.

item.title: Uma ameaça persistente e silenciosa desafia a campanha de Lula
item.description: Lula regained polling momentum after a R$200+ billion benefits package, leading Flávio Bolsonaro by 10 points in the first round and 6 in the second, with improved government approval and gains among undecided voters. However, the persistent silent threat of rising living costs endangers his support: 44% believe the economy worsened over the past year and 69% report higher food prices, threatening his appeal among non-ideologically aligned voters. Lula’s 53% rejection rate remains high, and the risk of backlash over food inflation echoes what damaged Bolsonaro in 2022.

item.title: Militante de esquerda confirma ameaças de morte a candidato a governador do RS
item.description: Federal deputy Luciano Zucco (PL-RS), pre-candidate for governor of Rio Grande do Sul, received death threats from a left-wing profile identified as Cleomar dos Santos, a bag store employee from Novo Hamburgo. The messages included explicit threats like 'I missed the chance to burst your head' and were politically motivated. After a legislative police investigation, the perpetrator confessed, expressed regret, and Zucco now receives round-the-clock security due to rising political violence in Brazil.

item.title: Cotada para Fazenda se licencia de empresa por campanha de Flávio
item.description: Economist Daniella Marques took a leave from Legend, a wealth management firm, to join Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential pre-campaign. She is being considered for the Ministry of Finance and is expected to help shape the government plan, engage with financial markets, and strengthen outreach to female voters. The move follows a communication team overhaul that saw Marcello Lopes replaced by Eduardo Fischer and Alexandre Oltramari.

item.title: Nunes Marques rejeita pedido para barrar filme sobre Bolsonaro durante período eleitoral
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques of the TSE rejected a request by Lula allies to ban the screening of 'Dark Horse', a Bolsonaro biopic, during the 2026 electoral period. The ruling cited lack of standing, as the petitioners are not running for national office like the subject of the film, Flávio Bolsonaro. The petition also demanded financial transparency, referencing reports that Flávio Bolsonaro sought $24 million in funding for the film.

item.title: Dez ‘Brasis’ para bancar o governo Lula
item.description: The Lula government faces criticism for promoting populist measures in Congress, such as reducing the workweek, labeled irresponsible and electorally motivated. The text denounces the hypocrisy of government officials who condemn 'electoral handouts' while supporting proposals with uncalculated economic impacts. The narrative suggests these actions aim solely to secure political support to sustain the government.

item.title: Em vídeo à seleção brasileira, Lula pede “raça” e “concentração”
item.description: President Lula urged the Brazilian national team to play with grit, will, commitment, and team spirit in the 2026 World Cup, emphasizing the players’ peripheral origins and urging them to rise after setbacks. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro also posted a video accusing the Lula government of trying to 'steal' Brazil’s flag, claiming he 'rescued' it from the trash and using the national symbol to rally political support.

item.title: Produtora de “Dark Horse” avalia adiar o lançamento do filme
item.description: Go Up Entertainment is considering delaying the release of the film 'Dark Horse,' about the life of Jair Bolsonaro, to avoid association with the 2026 elections, as advised by lawyer Ricardo Sayeg. The film had a declared investment of R$ 75 million, tied to a judicial investigation involving the ICB — an institute linked to the producer’s owner — accused of diverting funds from a São Paulo City Hall contract.

item.title: Petrobras e Pemex vão assinar acordo de cooperação em junho, diz Magda
item.description: Petrobras and Pemex will sign a memorandum of understanding in June to establish initial cooperation in exploration and production, refining, petrochemicals, and data sharing. The announcement was made by Petrobras president Magda Chambriard during the reinauguration of the company’s headquarters in Rio de Janeiro, following a meeting between Lula and Sheinbaum discussing a potential deepwater agreement.

item.title: Como pedido de Bolsonaro para anular trama golpista afetou demais condenados
item.description: The defense strategy of Jair Bolsonaro to annul his conviction for involvement in a coup plot was viewed with skepticism by lawyers of other convicted individuals, who fear the appeal could be used as a political tool in favorable moments, such as after the 2026 elections. The initiative faces significant legal hurdles, as it requires the judiciary to admit error in its own ruling — considered highly unlikely. Moreover, the current political climate, marked by heightened tensions and pressure on the STF, reduces the likelihood of an impartial review.

item.title: Lula pede que seleção jogue com ‘alma’ na estreia contra o Marrocos na Copa
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva released a video urging the Brazilian national team to play with 'soul' in their World Cup opener against Morocco, emphasizing the importance of playing for the Brazilian people and youth. He addressed coach Carlo Ancelotti, praising his experience as a player and coach, and urged the team to persevere through setbacks, stressing that scoring goals is what truly matters. Lula also said Ancelotti could become a hero like Feola, Zagallo, and Felipão, stating that Brazil does not play the World Cup to lose, but to win.

item.title: Esquerda ou direita? Estudo inédito mostra quem domina as redes no Brasil
item.description: A study by Ativaweb Datalab reveals that the right dominates social media in Brazil, with X (9.4/10) and TikTok (9.0/10) as its strongest platforms, while the left balances the playing field on Instagram. The Digital Right scores 82.4 points versus 74.8 for the Digital Left, showing a significant advantage in virality and organic mobilization. The left’s main challenge is adapting its language to new content formats, as the 2026 election will be heavily influenced by algorithms and the ability to capture and retain public attention.

item.title: Julia Zanatta surge como cotada para vice do Flávio Bolsonaro nas Eleições 2026
item.description: Julia Zanatta, a state deputy from Paraná representing the Liberal Party (PL), is being discussed as a potential vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket for the 2026 elections. Her name has gained traction within Bolsonarist circles due to her close ties with former President Jair Bolsonaro and her conservative policy stance. A potential Bolsonaro-Zanatta ticket would aim to solidify support from evangelical and right-wing voters in Paraná and across Brazil.

item.title: PRD e Solidariedade confirmam apoio à reeleição de Tarcísio em SP
item.description: The PRD-Solidariedade federation confirmed its support for the re-election of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) in São Paulo, during a meeting in the state capital attended by Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB). The endorsement was described as crucial for the re-election campaign, with national federation president Ovasco Resende stating the party would be on the ticket and provide 'all necessary support'. The decision dashed hopes of former Santo André mayor Paulo Serra (PSDB), who had been negotiating with Solidariedade for a potential gubernatorial run.

item.title: Como recompensa a ‘sacríficio’, PT oferece ‘terreno na lua’ em eventual Lula 4
item.description: The PT is offering federal positions as a reward for leaders willing to run in high-risk candidacies in 2026 to strengthen Lula’s presidential ticket in key states. Despite promises of ministerial roles or other government posts, several figures — including Rodrigo Pacheco, Marina Silva, and Márcio França — have declined, opting instead for safer races like Senate bids. This resistance is hindering the formation of competitive slates in São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Goiás, and Espírito Santo.

item.title: Desgaste de Flávio não impulsiona outros nomes da oposição, diz diretor da Quaest
item.description: The Quaest poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro losing ground in the presidential race, yet his decline is not boosting other opposition figures. Director Felipe Nunes says this reflects a deadlock in Brazil's right and center-right.
